Alex — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the PoC scope and technical approach.

High-level recap from discovery:
- Goal: Integrate Redwood inference into ApSeed’s insights pipeline to power structured recommendations + on-demand function calls for enrichment.
- Primary constraints: PII-sensitive customer records (redaction required), on-prem connector for some data, strict latency targets (95th < 450ms for API surface).

Proposed technical scope for PoC (MVP):
1) SDK quickstart + auth: recommend service-account JWTs scoped to a dedicated Redwood Private deployment (can discuss API-key fallback for hosted).
2) Routing: route by request metadata to either low-latency model variant (for interactive flows) or cost-optimized variant (batch).
3) Structured output + tool calling: enforce JSON schema in model responses; tool definitions exposed as OpenAPI endpoints that Redwood can call.
4) Embeddings + reranker: local embedding store with k-NN retrieval followed by a lightweight reranker model.
5) Error handling: deterministic fallbacks for tool failures, circuit-breaker + retry for transient tool errors.

Open items / asks from your side:
- Sample payloads (anonymized) and an example enrichment tool API spec (OpenAPI/Swagger).
- Confirmation on auth preference (service account JWT vs. API key + KMS).
- Any network constraints (VPC peering, IP allowlist).

Next steps / timeline:
- Internal SE design: Redwood to produce an integration playbook (this thread). — by 2026-06-16
- PoC kick-off call: schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive w/ ApSeed engineers — target week of 2026-06-22
- Goal: PoC complete with acceptance criteria by 2026-07-02

Attachments: apseed-integration-requirements.xlsx (sheet: mvp-requirements) and apseed-arch-sketch.png

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internal owners once we confirm your availability.

— Priyom

Thanks Priyom — solid summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

Constraints / preferences:
- PII: We cannot send raw customer identifiers to third parties. Any payloads must be hashed or tokenized; where possible we’ll provide synthetic/anonymized examples for the PoC.
- Auth: preference for service-account JWTs with keys rotated through our KMS. API keys are acceptable only for internal dev environments.
- Network: we’ll need to test both SaaS-hosted (for speed) and Private/VPC (for sensitive workloads). VPC option requires static egress IPs for allowlisting.

Technical asks:
- For embeddings: we plan to host a vector store in our cloud account and would prefer Redwood to accept vectors via an S3-backed import or an API push. Can you confirm supported import options?
- For tool calls: example workflows will include calling internal enrichment services (e.g., customer_enrich GET /v1/enrich/{id}) and a third-party pricing service. We need deterministic error semantics — if tool X fails, we must not return partial recommendations.

We’ll attach our internal requirements sheet (I’ll forward the full spec after cleaning PII).

Alex

Alex / Priyom — looping in a proposed technical pattern based on your constraints. I sketched both a quick PoC path and a production-hardened option.

Quick PoC (minimal changes):
- Auth: issue a service-account JWT for Redwood with a scoped role. Exchange via KMS-managed keypair in ApSeed account.
- SDK: Redwood’s JS/py SDK supports a bootstrap flow: configure base_url, auth_token, schema enforcement toggle.
- Embeddings: Push-based import (S3 or bulk API). For PoC we can accept an S3 manifest with hashed IDs.
- Tool definitions: provide an OpenAPI 3.0 description for each enrichment tool; Redwood will call those endpoints on behalf of the model.

Production pattern (recommended):
1) Routing & model variants:
   - Requests carry metadata: {customer_tier, use_case, latency_budget}. Router uses policy table to select model variant + endpoint (private vs hosted).
2) Tool/function calling pattern (definition):
   - Tool = {name, input_schema, output_schema, endpoint, semantically_idempotent_flag, timeout_ms, retry_policy}.
   - We recommend declaring semantically_idempotent_flag for enrichment tools so retries are safe.
3) Tool choice and ordering:
   - Intent-classifier -> candidate-tools -> reranker (ML reranker or deterministic scoring based on recency/trust).
   - For deterministic enrichment, prefer synchronous calls for small number of tools; for larger fanout use async worker + aggregation pattern.
4) Parallel tools & aggregator:
   - Fanout up to N parallel tool calls (configurable per-route). Each call returns {status, payload, trace_id}. Aggregator enforces schema and applies an aggregation policy (first-success, merge-by-priority, consensus).
5) Error handling & fallbacks:
   - Transient errors: exponential backoff + limited retries (respect semantically_idempotent flag).
   - Persistent/tool-unavailable: fallback to cached enrichment or a basic deterministic rule.
   - Circuit-breaker: open after X failures in Y window; route to fallback variant.
   - Observability: attach per-tool latency and error metrics; expose traces in Redwood Console.

Structured output enforcement:
- We recommend model responses be validated against a JSON Schema. Redwood can perform server-side enforcement and return a validation failure reason.

Small example of a tool definition (text-only):
- name: customer_enrich
- input_schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"}}}
- output_schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"score":{"type":"number"},"segments":{"type":"array"}}}
- endpoint: https://internal.apseed.com/api/enrich
- semantically_idempotent_flag: true

Notes on embeddings + reranker:
- Retrieval: store vectors in your vector DB; Redwood will accept top-k vectors or IDs and then call a reranker model endpoint.
- Reranker: lightweight cross-encoder tuned on your relevance labels; we can host or provide a managed variant.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short arch sketch and the PoC checklist.
